newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Feb customs-cleared trade.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan Feb customs-cleared trade.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus rose 6.5 percent in February from a year earlier to 686.72 billion yen, the first rise in the surplus since November 1994, the Finance Ministry said on Monday.
JASON JAMES, STRATEGIST, HSBC JAMES CAPEL

"I think (these figures) are certainly indicating that the trend is starting to change. We should be seeing from now on the Japanese surplus starting to pick up fairly steadily and starting to contribute positively to Japanese growth instead of negatively."
MASARU TAKAGI, CHIEF ECONOMIST, FUJI RESEARCH INSTITUTE

"(The surplus) brings a plus impact on the Japanese economy -- much more higher growth of Japanese exports, but relatively weak imports. But the Japanese sales tax is rising from three percent to five percent from April, so it's a minus and a plus situation. So I don't know where the Japanese economy is going, but from today's figures, it's a very good impact on the real economy."
"Everybody is looking at these numbers from a year-on-year basis but in fact it's been increasing since the spring of 1996 if you look at the seasonally adjusted numbers.

"This should start to exert upward pressure on the yen as awareness grows that the surplus is rising again. I think we have seen the peak in the exchange rate for the moment in terms of dollar strength."
